<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Spring Boot 4 has different artifact names - spring-boot-starter-webmvc instead of web, and separate test starters.

The Maven build needs the maven-enforcer-plugin configured for Java 21.

AssertJ will be added explicitly if the modular test starters do not include it.

The V1 migration will use H2 in PostgreSQL compatibility mode. It will define the tickets table with all columns, constraints, and a sequence starting at 1001. JPA entities are next.

Ticket will use @Version for optimistic locking. Comment will have a ManyToOne relationship to Ticket. Status and priority will be STRING enums. Timestamps will rely on database defaults or lifecycle callbacks.

PublicTicketId will be omitted to avoid inventing domain fields outside the requested scope. The Ticket entity will use a String public_id field instead. The repository layer is next.

TicketRepository will expose findByPublicId and a paged list ordered by updatedAt descending, then id descending. CommentRepository will find comments by ticket ordered by createdAt and id. A PublicIdSequence component will be added to the repository package to support public ID generation, as required by the implementation plan.

The migration will include a TicketIngestion table but no entity for it. Configuration will use application.yml and application-test.yml with ddl-auto set to validate and Flyway enabled. The test profile will use an in-memory H2 database in PostgreSQL mode.

Ticket will use a OneToMany relationship with lazy fetch for comments. Comment will use a LAZY ManyToOne to Ticket. Lombok will be avoided in favor of standard Java with explicit getters, setters, and a no-arg constructor. The Ticket entity will contain id, publicId, title, description, status, priority, assignee, category, resolutionNotes, version, createdAt, and updatedAt. The Comment entity will contain id, ticket, author, content, and createdAt. TicketStatus will have OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED, and CANCELLED. TicketPriority will have LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, and CRITICAL.

Enum parsing methods will reject unknown values. The test plan includes context load tests, entity invariant tests, DataJpaTest for persistence, and integration tests for both repositories. The V1 migration SQL is being drafted with H2-compatible syntax.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I'll create all files. Let me write the V1 migration SQL carefully.

H2 in PostgreSQL mode supports TIMESTAMPTZ or TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE for timestamp columns.

H2 PostgreSQL mode supports BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY for auto-increment columns. The pom.xml will enforce Java 21 via the maven-enforcer-plugin. Flyway will be included through the Spring Boot 4 starter. Empty license blocks will be removed for cleanliness. The existing modular test dependencies will be kept.

Migration constraints will enforce non-empty assignee values and require resolution notes for resolved or closed tickets. Entities will use snake_case table names and jakarta.persistence annotations. The version field will be annotated with @Version, and comments will link to tickets via @JoinColumn.

PrePersist and PreUpdate callbacks will set timestamps on entities. Comment entities will only set createdAt. Setters will trim strings and convert blank assignees to null. Tests will use the @ActiveProfiles("test") annotation. The application.yml structure is being drafted.

The application.yml now defines the H2 PostgreSQL datasource with file-based persistence and a test profile using an in-memory H2 database. Hibernate DDL validation is enabled, and the H2 console is disabled.
</details></think>

Fix Comment entity - comment repository test saves comment without proper ticket association on first save.

Comment.setTicket is package-private, so repository tests cannot call it. Adding a factory method on Comment that accepts a Ticket would resolve this.

Making Comment.setTicket public is the simpler fix for JPA bidirectional mapping. TicketEntityTest indentation also needs correction. Then run mvn verify.

TicketRepositoryIntegrationTest has an ordering issue. The sequenceStartsAt1001 test assumes the sequence starts at 1001, but persistsWithDefaults may consume sequence numbers first. JUnit 5 does not guarantee method order. I will either add @TestMethodOrder or isolate the sequence test in a separate class with @DirtiesContext.

H2 sequences do not roll back with @Transactional. Sequence values persist across test methods in the same Spring context. The sequence test should assert only that IDs increment correctly, not exact starting values. A dedicated test class running first would also prevent gaps.
</details></think>

The `backend/` tree was empty, so the foundation was scaffolded from Spring Initializr (Boot **4.0.0**, Java **21**) and wired to match `spec/data-model.md` and the package rules in `.cursor/rules/java-springboot.mdc`.

## What was implemented

| Area | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Build** | `backend/pom.xml`, Maven wrapper, Java 21 enforcer (`[21,22)`), starters: webmvc, data-jpa, validation, Flyway, H2 |
| **Config** | `application.yml` — H2 PostgreSQL mode, `ddl-auto: validate`, Flyway on; profiles `test` (in-memory) and `local` (file DB + H2 console) |
| **Migrations** | `V1__baseline.sql` — `ticket_public_seq` (start 1001), `tickets`, `comments`, `ticket_ingestion` with constraints/indexes from the spec |
| **Domain** | `Ticket`, `Comment`, `TicketStatus`, `TicketPriority` — no Lombok; LAZY associations; `@Version` on tickets; trim/blank rules in setters |
| **Repositories** | `TicketRepository`, `CommentRepository`, `PublicIdSequence` (for `TKT-*` ids per data model §4.3) |

No controllers or RAG code were added. The `ticket_ingestion` table is in the migration only (entity/repo left for a later task).

## Tests

- Unit: `TicketStatusTest`, `TicketPriorityTest`, `TicketEntityTest`
- Integration: `TicketManagementApplicationTests`, `TicketRepositoryIntegrationTest`, `CommentRepositoryIntegrationTest`

## Build result

```text
./mvnw verify   → BUILD SUCCESS
./mvnw test     → Tests run: 14, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
```

## Notes / follow-ups

1. **Flyway + H2** — Startup logs a warning that H2 **2.4.240** is newer than Flyway’s last verified H2 version (2.3.232). Migrations still applied successfully; keep an eye on future Flyway releases if this becomes noisy in CI.
2. **Mockito / JDK** — Mockito self-attach and dynamic agent warnings on Java 21; tests pass; optional Mockito agent config per their docs if you want to silence this later.
3. **Not in this task** — `TicketIngestion` JPA entity, schema constraint integration tests (T2.1), `application-local.yml` split file, root `.gitignore` for `backend/data/`.

Suggested next step on the plan: **T3.4** (`TicketIngestion` + repository) or **T1.2** (`@ConfigurationProperties`). Say which you want to tackle next.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I made a mistake in TicketController - assigneeProvided logic is wrong.

The assigneeProvided logic needs to handle Jackson partial updates correctly.

Records cannot distinguish a null assignee from an omitted field. A mutable UpdateTicketRequest class with a boolean flag will handle partial updates correctly.

A custom `@JsonProperty` setter on `UpdateTicketRequest` can detect null assignee values during deserialization. Using `Map<String, Object>` or an explicit `Boolean assigneePresent` flag were rejected as poor alternatives.

The `@JsonSetter` approach on `UpdateTicketRequest` will set a boolean flag when the assignee field is present in the JSON, even if the value is null. This correctly distinguishes an explicit null from an omitted key. The `containsAssigneeKey` helper method will be removed. `CommentController` also needs to be fixed.

Ticket creation will return an empty comments list since the created entity lacks comment data. GlobalExceptionHandler needs its unused WebRequest import removed. TicketStatusService must ignore resolution notes on non-RESOLVED transitions per the API contract. TicketRepositoryIntegrationTest needs fixing for the list method. CommentController implementation is next.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Two issues:
1. ObjectMapper not autowired - use new ObjectMapper() in test or remove autowire and parse manually

2. State machine test - allowed count might be wrong.

The state machine matrix contains exactly 5 allowed transitions between different statuses. The test failure likely stems from the assertion reading the wrong value.

The state machine test failure stems from same-status pairs. The `isAllowed` method returns false for identical statuses, so those 5 pairs are neither counted as allowed nor rejected. This leaves the allowed count at 4 instead of 5.

The test expects 20 rejected transitions, but the actual count is 15. The 5 same-status pairs are excluded from the rejected tally because `isAllowed` returns false for identical statuses. The spec requires 25 total cells, 5 allowed, and 20 rejected including same-status. The test logic must be updated to count all non-allowed transitions as rejected.
</details></think>

Implemented ticket management end-to-end per the specs (no RAG pipeline). Summary:

## Implemented

### Domain & state machine
- `TicketStateMachine` — pure 5×5 transition table; illegal moves throw `InvalidTransitionException` (**HTTP 400** / `INVALID_TRANSITION`)
- `PublicTicketId` — path validation (`TKT-<digits>`)

### Services
- **`TicketService`** — create, get, list (search + status filter + paging), partial update (assignee clear via `"assignee": null`)
- **`TicketStatusService`** — transitions with resolution-note rules; optimistic-lock → **409**
- **`CommentService`** — append-only comments; terminal tickets → **409**; version bump via `OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT`
- **`TicketValidator`** — A-07 limits, categories, `UNASSIGNED` assignee, LIKE escaping for `%`/`_`
- **`IngestionRequestWriter`** + `TicketIngestion` — ingestion rows on writes (worker not implemented)

### REST (`spec/api-contract.md`)
| Method | Path |
|--------|------|
| GET | `/api/tickets` (`q`, `status`, `page`, `size`) |
| POST | `/api/tickets` |
| GET | `/api/tickets/{publicId}` (includes `allowedTransitions`) |
| PUT | `/api/tickets/{publicId}` |
| POST | `/api/tickets/{publicId}/status` |
| POST | `/api/tickets/{publicId}/comments` |

### Web layer
- Request/response DTOs, `TicketMapper`, `GlobalExceptionHandler` (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `INVALID_TRANSITION`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`)
- Config: `app.tickets.*` in `application.yml`

## Tests (31 total)

| Area | Tests |
|------|--------|
| State machine matrix | `TicketStateMachineTest` |
| Validation | `TicketValidatorTest` |
| HTTP / persistence | `TicketApiIntegrationTest` (transitions, terminal, comments, search, 404/400) |
| Service + DB | `TicketServiceIntegrationTest` |
| Prior foundation tests | entities, repositories, context load |

## Build

```text
./mvnw verify  →  BUILD SUCCESS
Tests run: 31, Failures: 0, Errors: 0
```

## Notes
- Invalid transitions are **400**, never 409 (conflict reserved for terminal edits and lock loss).
- RAG worker, retrieval, and `POST /api/ai/ask` are **not** implemented.
- Spring Boot 4 MockMvc uses `org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureMockMvc` (not the Boot 3 package).
- `spring-boot-starter-test` was added for AssertJ/Mockito alongside the Boot 4 modular test starters.

Next logical step: OpenAPI/springdoc parity (`T5.6`) or the RAG phases when you are ready.

Implement embedding and vector ingestion pipeline

spec/architecture.md

spec/rag-ingestion.md

spec/data-model.md

.cursor/rules/rag-vector-store.mdc

Implement:

Ticket knowledge document generation.

Description extraction.

Comment extraction.

Resolution information extraction.

Paragraph-aware chunking.

Metadata enrichment.

Embedding generation.

Vector-store persistence.

Automatic re-ingestion after ticket updates.

Automatic re-ingestion after comments and relevant status changes.

Required metadata:

ticketId

status

priority

assignee

category

Technical requirements:

Use a genuine embedding model.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I need to implement a comprehensive but focused RAG pipeline.

The implementation plan targets Spring AI BOM 2.0.2 and Ollama. It defines RagProperties and a dedicated rag package. The package covers chunking, ticket extraction, snapshot reading, vector indexing, backoff, ingestion scheduling, and metrics.

Configuration classes for vector stores and embeddings will be added. The ingestion repository will query due rows. Ticket transaction wake-ups will use TransactionSynchronization. Embedding models will switch by Spring profile: Ollama in production and a lightweight test model in tests.

A `TestFixtureEmbeddingModel` will generate valid 768-dimensional vectors for test wiring. It will be used only in non-production profiles. Live Ollama tests will be gated by an environment variable.

The requirement for a genuine embedding model means production code must call EmbeddingModel.embed() rather than generating vectors internally. The test embedding model must therefore be a real Spring AI EmbeddingModel bean, not a synthetic one.

The test embedding strategy is being refined. A SentenceTransformers model was rejected as too heavy. Instead, the same OllamaEmbeddingModel bean will be used across all profiles. In tests, the base URL will be mocked via WireMock or @MockBean. Integration tests will still exercise the real embedding flow.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Good - `new FilterExpressionBuilder().eq("ticketId", "TKT-1001").build().build()` - probably `.build()` returns Expression.

Old chunks will be deleted using a filter on ticketId and ingestVersion. The ingestVersion metadata is stored as a string.

Chunk records will hold id, text, body, and metadata. TicketSnapshot will bundle ticket fields, comments, and version. TicketDocumentExtractor and TicketChunker will use RagProperties for chunk size and overlap. ContentHash will be SHA-256 hex of UTF-8 body. Null assignees map to UNASSIGNED. IngestionProcessor.processOne will run snapshot reads in a read-only transaction and keep embedding generation outside the transaction.

The ingestion worker will load the row, read the snapshot, chunk and embed documents outside the transaction, then commit the ingestion row update and delete old versions outside the transaction. Failures will trigger backoff on the ticket_ingestion table. A scheduled poller will call the worker at fixed intervals. An IngestionWakeUp mechanism will handle wake-up events.

The wake-up mechanism will submit the worker to a single-thread executor. An IndexReconciler will initialize ingestion rows for all tickets on startup and reset their indexed versions to null. It will mark tickets as pending and remove them from the readiness set once indexing completes. IngestionMetrics will count statuses from the repository. Unit tests will cover ChunkIdFactory, TicketDocumentExtractor, and TicketChunker.

An integration test will create a ticket, wait for ingestion, update the title, and verify that the indexed chunks reflect the new title. Deterministic fake embeddings will allow exact text matching in similarity searches. The test will query the knowledge index by ticketId and compare chunk counts and metadata. The POM will also add spring-ai-bom 2.0.2 to its dependencyManagement.

The POM will import the Spring AI BOM 2.0.2 and declare explicit dependencies on spring-ai-starter-model-ollama and spring-ai-vector-store.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

The RAG ingestion pipeline is in place and **`./mvnw verify` passes (35 tests)**. Below is what was built and what was fixed to get tests green.

## Pipeline (per spec)

| Stage | Implementation |
|--------|----------------|
| Document generation | `TicketDocumentExtractor` — description, comments, resolution notes |
| Chunking | `ChunkSplitter` + `TicketChunker` (paragraph-aware, overlap from `app.rag.chunk.*`) |
| Metadata | `ticketId`, `status`, `priority`, `assignee` (`UNASSIGNED`), `category`, `kind`, `ingestVersion`, `contentHash`, `title`, etc. |
| Embeddings | **Prod/default:** Ollama `nomic-embed-text` via Spring AI. **Tests:** `@Profile("test")` `TestEmbeddingConfig` (768-dim semantic-style vectors, not zeros/hashes) |
| Vector store | `SimpleVectorStore` + `KnowledgeIndex` / `SimpleKnowledgeIndex` |
| Stale / duplicate control | Versioned chunks; `deleteTicketVersionNot` after successful index; idempotent version check in `IngestionProcessor` |
| Auto re-ingestion | `IngestionRequestWriter` on create/update; `CommentService` / `TicketStatusService`; post-commit `IngestionWakeUp` + `IngestionScheduler` |
| Observability / retry | `IngestionOutcomeWriter`, backoff (`app.rag.ingestion.*`), `IngestionMetrics`, failure logging |
| Startup backfill | `IndexReconciler` queues all tickets on `ApplicationReadyEvent` |

Configuration is in `application.yml` / `RagProperties` (`top-k`, `similarity-threshold`, chunk sizes, poll interval, backoff).

## Tests

- **Unit:** `TicketDocumentExtractorTest`, `TicketChunkerTest`, `ChunkIdFactoryTest`
- **Integration:** `IngestionPipelineIntegrationTest` — create → ingest → update title → vector docs show `Beta title` and a single `ingestVersion`

## Fixes applied this session

1. **Test profile:** Exclude Ollama auto-config so CI does not need a local Ollama daemon.
2. **`VectorStoreConfig`:** `@EventListener` limited to one parameter (injected `EmbeddingModel` + `RagProperties`).
3. **`IngestionRequestWriter`:** `ticketRepository.flush()` before reading `@Version`, so `requested_version` matches the committed ticket version (this was blocking re-ingestion).
4. **`IngestionWorker`:** Re-run when woken while already processing (avoids dropped wake-ups under test concurrency).

## Running locally with real embeddings

Start Ollama with `nomic-embed-text` on `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (see `spring.ai.ollama` in `application.yml`). Use the `local` profile or default datasource as documented in the repo.

Retrieval (`POST /api/ai/ask`) is still not implemented; this work is ingestion and indexing only. Say if you want that layer next.

Document has getScore() - perfect.

Beginning full implementation. Creating a worktree on a branch per project rules. No commit is needed.

A `PromptBuilder` will assemble the system and user messages. The `AskResult` record will carry the final answer, a grounding flag, the citations, and the outcome. ## `POST /api/ai/ask`

### API
- **`AiController`** — `POST /api/ai/ask` with `AskRequest` / `AskResponse` / `CitationResponse` (matches `spec/rag-api-contract.md`).
- **503** `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` when the index is rebuilding or the chat model fails/times out (`AssistantUnavailableException`).
- **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` for blank or over-limit questions (before embed/chat).

### Orchestration (single retrieval → generation path)
`AskService` validates → checks `IndexReadiness` → `RetrievalService` → if empty, exact **`No relevant tickets found.`** (no LLM) → `PromptBuilder` → `ChatModel` (timeout from `app.rag.ask.timeout`) → `CitationValidator` → on failure, fail-closed to the same no-match body (`CITATION_REJECTED` logged) → `CitationSnippets` for server-built citations.

### Retrieval
- Similarity search with **`app.rag.top-k`**, **`app.rag.similarity-threshold`**, candidate over-fetch multiplier.
- **Visibility rule** (`ChunkVisibilityFilter`): ticket exists and `ingestVersion == indexed_version`.
- **Named ticket IDs** in the question (`TicketIdExtractor`): direct lookup, included even below threshold.
- Context capped by **`app.rag.context.max-chars`**.

### Grounding
- Fixed system prompt: context-only, `[ticket:<id>]` citations, no invented IDs, context is data not instructions.
- **`CitationValidator`**: every `[ticket:…]` must be in the retrieved set; at least one citation required.
- Citations/snippets come from retrieved chunks only (highest score per ticket, 300-char snippet).

### Configuration
- `app.rag.context.max-chars`, `app.rag.ask.question-max`, `app.rag.ask.timeout`
- `spring.ai.ollama.chat.options.model` (default `llama3.2`) for non-test profiles
- Test profile: Ollama chat excluded; **`ScriptableTestChatModel`** (`TestChatConfig`) for deterministic answers

### Key files
| Area | Files |
|------|--------|
| HTTP | `web/AiController.java`, `web/dto/AskRequest.java`, `AskResponse.java`, `CitationResponse.java` |
| RAG | `rag/AskService.java`, `RetrievalService.java`, `PromptBuilder.java`, `CitationValidator.java`, `CitationSnippets.java`, `ChunkVisibilityFilter.java`, `TicketIdExtractor.java`, … |
| Errors | `domain/AssistantUnavailableException.java`, `GlobalExceptionHandler` |

---

**`AskApiIntegrationTest` covers:** grounded relevant Q, irrelevant/no-match (no chat), invented citation fail-closed, uncited answer fail-closed, empty corpus no-match, blank question 400.

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Implemented a separate Next.js app in `frontend/` aligned with `spec/ui-flow.md`, `spec/api-contract.md`, and `spec/rag-api-contract.md`.

## What was built

| Area | Implementation |
|------|----------------|
| **Routes** | `/` → `/tickets`, `/tickets/new`, `/tickets/[ticketId]` |
| **List** | Search + status filter (URL: `q`, `status`, `page`, `size`), pagination, empty states, loading/error |
| **Create / edit** | `TicketForm`, field errors from API, cancel with confirm on create |
| **Detail** | Meta fields, description, resolution notes, terminal notice |
| **Status** | `allowedTransitions`, resolve flow with required notes |
| **Comments** | Timeline (oldest first), author remembered in `sessionStorage` |
| **Assistant** | Drawer (stays open on navigation), `POST /api/ai/ask`, sources **only** from `citations`, no-match as info style, 503 as error |
| **API** | Typed client under `src/lib/api/`; proxies via `next.config.ts` rewrites to `BACKEND_URL` |

## Reusable pieces

`Button`, `Spinner`, `ErrorBanner`, `InfoBanner`, `FieldError`, `AppChrome`, ticket/assistant components under `src/components/`.

## Checks run (actual results)

| Command | Result |
|---------|--------|
| `npm run lint` | **Pass** (no errors) |
| `npm run typecheck` | **Pass** |
| `npm run test` | **5 tests passed** (3 files: `errors.test.ts`, `client.test.ts`, `AssistantDrawer.test.ts`) |
| `npm run build` | **Pass** (routes: `/`, `/tickets`, `/tickets/new`, `/tickets/[ticketId]`) |

## How to run

```bash
cd backend && ./mvnw spring-boot:run   # :8080
cd frontend && cp .env.example .env.local && npm run dev   # :3000
```

The UI is not end-to-end verified against a live backend in this session; API calls work when the Spring app is up and reachable through the rewrite.
